NJ-2026-S687.title: Creates Joint Blue Ribbon Task Force on Impacts of Climate Change on Property Insurance.

actions.text: Substituted for A4560 (1R)
Motion To Aa (Kanitra)
Motion To Table (Greenwald) (43-24-0)
Passed by the Assembly (55-22-2)
Reported out of Assembly Comm. with Amendments, 2nd Reading
Passed by the Senate (36-2)
Received in the Assembly, Referred to Assembly Environment and Solid Waste Committee
Reported from Senate Committee, 2nd Reading
Introduced in the Senate, Referred to Senate Environment and Energy Committee

NJ-2026-S687.aiSummary: The bill would create a 17-member task force in the Department of Banking and Insurance to study how climate change affects home and business property insurance in New Jersey. Its members would include state officials, lawmakers, private sector representatives, nonprofit members, and academics with climate and insurance knowledge. The task force would review issues like insurance costs, coverage, risk, and access, then submit a report with findings and recommendations within one year after all members are appointed.

NJ-2026-A5735.title: Authorizes establishment of seasonal pedestrian malls.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly Tourism, Gaming and the Arts Committee

NJ-2026-A5735.aiSummary: The bill would let New Jersey towns set up seasonal pedestrian malls for a set time of year, with temporary or moveable features. It would allow a town to start studies, then pass an ordinance to create one if the area meets the law’s rules. Owners of land directly next to the proposed mall would get notice before the hearing.

NJ-2026-A5730.title: Requires pharmacies to provide emergency 30-day supply of insulin in certain circumstances.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly Financial Institutions and Insurance Committee

NJ-2026-A5730.aiSummary: The bill would let people in urgent need of insulin get a one-time emergency 30-day supply through a pharmacy, using an application made by the state health insurance department and the Board of Pharmacy. It would apply to New Jersey residents who are not in NJ FamilyCare or a similar program, and who do not have insulin coverage that keeps their out-of-pocket cost at $35 or less for a 30-day supply. Pharmacies could seek payment from the insulin maker or its vendor, and the bill would take effect 180 days after it is enacted.

NJ-2026-A5726.title: "Micro-Reactor Incentive Act"; directs BPU to request proposals to construct micro nuclear reactors in State.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly Telecommunications and Utilities Committee

NJ-2026-A5726.aiSummary: The bill would direct the Board of Public Utilities to set up a competitive process to award incentives for building micro nuclear reactors in New Jersey. It would let the board seek proposals from projects that start after the bill takes effect and connect to a New Jersey power system or serve only New Jersey facilities. The bill also sets rules for bidding, worker pay during construction, and a report to lawmakers within four years after the law takes effect.

NJ-2026-A5721.title: Requires State Board of Education to promulgate certain regulations concerning special education complaint investigations and corrective action plans.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly Education Committee

NJ-2026-A5721.aiSummary: The bill would require the State Board of Education to set rules for how the Office of Special Education handles special education complaints. It would require more sharing of documents with the person who filed the complaint, a chance to respond, and a fuller report that lists the evidence used. It would also require public posting of the complaint guide and a form for parents or guardians to ask for help enforcing a corrective action plan, and it would add data tracking to show when each noncompliance problem is fixed.

NJ-2026-A5717.title: Requires DOE to publish special education complaint investigation reports and provide links to certain relevant court decisions.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly Education Committee

NJ-2026-A5717.aiSummary: The Department of Education would have to post special education complaint investigation reports on its website and keep a public database of special education legal decisions. It would also add links to later state or federal court decisions in those cases, and make the database searchable by things like the issue, the school district, and any award or corrective plan. The bill affects parents, school districts, school staff, and others who use special education records.

NJ-2026-A4740.title: "Safe Commercial Routes Act - Commercial Driver Human Trafficking Awareness Training"; requires applicants for commercial driver licenses and drivers renewing commercial driver licenses to complete human trafficking awareness training.

actions.text: Passed by the Assembly (79-0-0)
Assembly Floor Amendment Passed (Quijano) (Voice)
Reported out of Assembly Committee, 2nd Reading
Reported out of Asm. Comm. with Amendments, and Referred to Assembly Appropriations Committee
Introduced, Referred to Assembly Transportation and Independent Authorities Committee

NJ-2026-A4740.aiSummary: The bill would require people applying for a commercial driver license, and drivers renewing one, to complete human trafficking awareness training. It would have the Attorney General help develop, approve, review, and update the training course and approve who can provide it. Drivers would also have to certify that they finished the training and note the date and approved provider.

NJ-2026-A2210.title: Requires homemaker-home health aide and nursing assistant certification examinations to be translated into multiple languages.

actions.text: Passed by the Assembly (62-16-0)
Transferred to Assembly Aging and Human Services Committee
Reported out of Assembly Comm. with Amendments, 2nd Reading
Introduced, Referred to Assembly Regulated Professions Committee

NJ-2026-A2210.aiSummary: The bill would require nursing assistant and homemaker-home health aide certification tests to be offered in multiple languages. It would cover the Department of Health and the New Jersey Board of Nursing, and the tests would include languages such as English, Spanish, Haitian Creole, Tagalog, Arabic, Gujarati, and French, with more languages added as needed. The act would take effect on the first day of the sixth month after it is enacted.

NJ-2026-A1315.title: Modifies collective statewide transfer agreement and reverse transfer agreement; establishes New Jersey Transfer Ombudsperson within Office of Secretary of Higher Education.

actions.text: Passed by the Assembly (74-1-3)
Reported out of Assembly Committee, 2nd Reading
Reported and Referred to Assembly Appropriations Committee
Introduced, Referred to Assembly Higher Education Committee

NJ-2026-A1315.aiSummary: The bill would change New Jersey’s statewide rules for moving college credits between public colleges and universities. It would expand how credits from associate degrees, dual enrollment, and reverse transfer programs are handled, and it would set up an Ombudsperson in the Office of the Secretary of Higher Education to help with credit transfer issues. The ombudsperson would also collect data, review the agreement, and prepare an annual public report.
